{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVdzeZs8AAAABbXuYUQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bpi2wzhE8Jc0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bpi2w", "number": 1, "title": "Add collaboration templates, development/review/merge policies, and UI/UX layout principles", "body": "## Problem

This repository needs the same concise collaboration baseline used across the maintainer's other repositories: Issue/PR templates, development/review/merge guidance, an explicit collaboration-language convention, and discoverable UI/UX and layout principles.

The repository currently has an empty initialization commit on `main`. Inspect the current tree before implementation and preserve any useful content added meanwhile. Adapt the reference repositories' conventions to three-motionbricks rather than copying unrelated tooling, features or product assumptions.

## Expected outcome

Add one coherent, documentation-only baseline with these entry points:

- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md`
- `.github/pull_request_template.md`
- `docs/development-flow.md`
- `docs/review-guidelines.md`
- `AGENTS.md` linking contributors/AI agents to the canonical guidance
- `README.md` with a concise repository introduction, contribution links, and a canonical UI/UX and layout section

Equivalent existing paths may be reused if appropriate; avoid duplicate statements of the same policy.

### 1. Issue and PR templates

The Issue template should cover the problem, expected outcome, relevant context/reproduction, mandatory pre-merge acceptance criteria, optional validation, and genuinely required post-merge verification.

The PR template should cover the source Issue/problem, resulting behavior, focused changes, related Issues, validation actually performed, any remaining scope, and separately pending post-merge verification. Use closing keywords only when the implementation fully addresses the Issue; an intentionally partial PR must identify remaining work and keep the Issue open.

Use valid GitHub Issue-template metadata. No assignee/owner field is required. Do not add new CI workflows, repository settings, dependencies or application scaffolding for this documentation task.

### 2. Development, review and merge policy

Document the normal flow: **Issue → implementation → PR → review → revision as needed → merge**, followed by post-merge verification only when the Issue actually requires it.

- Treat the current Issue and relevant discussion as the scope reference. Choose the smallest coherent change that fully satisfies it.
- Check both missing requirements and unjustified additions. Avoid unrelated refactoring, speculative abstractions, frameworks and extra policies/configuration without a demonstrated need; simplicity must not excuse omitted requirements or necessary validation.
- Choose checks for the changed files and the repository's actual tooling. Report passes, failures, skips and unavailable checks honestly; do not invent commands or copy another repository's setup as if it existed here.
- Separate mandatory checks achievable before merge, optional validation, and genuinely post-merge-only checks. Default to criteria an AI implementer can execute and verify. Require human input, subjective review, physical hardware or external approval only when necessary to the actual Issue, explaining why and what result is needed.
- Fix agent-fixable findings and review the updated PR. Keep necessary human decisions and external dependencies distinct from code defects; report the concrete blocker instead of repeatedly requesting unchanged code fixes.
- Approve and merge only when the claimed scope is complete, relevant mandatory pre-merge checks pass, and no blocking findings or genuinely necessary unanswered questions remain. Follow the repository/workflow's existing merge authorization and target `main` unless the Issue says otherwise.
- Record required post-merge checks as pending until performed. A merge-triggered deployment/publication cannot be a pre-merge prerequisite, and pre-merge test results do not establish deployment success.
- For work owned by another managed repository, the default handoff is a linked `task` Issue in that repository. The current repository's Task should not create a cross-repository branch/PR unless explicitly instructed; the receiving repository's own Task workflow owns its implementation/review.

### 3. Collaboration language

Use **English** for newly authored templates, development/review/merge and UI/UX documentation, AI instructions, Issue/PR titles and bodies, review comments, and commit messages, consistent with the reference repositories.

This convention does not require translating historical material, changing product localization, or changing the language used in the maintainer's chat.

### 4. UI/UX and layout principles

Keep one short canonical section, preferably in README, with these three principles:

1. **Keep it simple.** Show only necessary information and actions; avoid unnecessary UI elements.
2. **Show, don't tell.** Prefer layout, spacing and visual hierarchy over explanatory labels or prose to communicate structure.
3. **Intuitive and predictable.** Keep appearance and behavior consistent with user expectations; don't interrupt the user's work.

Add concise, actionable layout guidance consistent with those principles:

- Give the primary content/result or preview clear visual priority where applicable; group related controls near what they affect and make the next useful action apparent.
- Use hierarchy, alignment, spacing and grouping to communicate relationships. Remove redundant headings, repeated helper copy and decorative status prose.
- Keep ordinary, necessary actions visible. Reveal contextual/advanced controls when relevant; do not hide everyday actions merely to make a screen sparse.
- Preserve readable responsive layouts, predictable navigation, keyboard operation, visible focus, accessible control names, meaningful labels and errors. “Show, don't tell” does not remove information needed to operate the interface.
- Keep necessary consent and destructive-action safeguards where applicable. Require a concrete user-facing reason for new controls, panels, steps or UI complexity.

Apply these as guidance for this repository's existing/future examples and user-facing surfaces without inventing a product design, adding a new GUI/design system, or changing runtime behavior in this Issue. Link the canonical section from review guidance so applicable UI changes are checked against it.

## Reference repositories

Read and adapt the relevant examples; these are references, not dependencies or text to copy wholesale:

- [mmd-gltf Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md)
- [mmd-gltf PR template](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md)
- [mmd-gltf development flow and English collaboration convention](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md)
- [mmd-gltf review and merge guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md)
- [mmd-gltf AI contributor entry point](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/AGENTS.md)
- [my-audio-to-text's three UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/README.md#uiux)
- [gen3d's layout and visibility guidance](https://github.com/takahirox/gen3d/blob/main/docs/ui-ux-guidelines.md)

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Usable Issue and PR templates cover the sections above, including actual validation and partial-scope handling.
- [ ] Development and review guidance consistently describes the full flow, bounded scope, review outcomes, merge criteria and separation of pre-/post-merge checks.
- [ ] The English collaboration convention is explicit and consistently referenced by templates and AI contributor guidance.
- [ ] One discoverable canonical UI/UX section states the three principles and concise layout guidance; review guidance links to it.
- [ ] README, AGENTS and templates point to the correct local documents/anchors, use this repository's name/URLs and contain no accidental copied project names, unsupported product/tooling claims or stale reference-specific Issue numbers.
- [ ] Validate Issue-template metadata, Markdown structure, relative links/anchors, consistency, and whitespace (`git diff --check`) using available tooling; review the complete diff including new files.
- [ ] This remains a documentation/templates change. No new application code, dependency, CI pipeline, design system, repository enforcement rule or unrelated refactor is introduced.

No runtime build, browser/hardware test, deployed-site check or human design approval is required for this documentation-only change. Future code changes must still perform their own applicable checks.

## Optional validation

None required.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.
